nary_nodes.label: Oil prices hit $100
evidence: Oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May as the escalating conflict in the Middle East reignited fears over global energy supplies.

nary_nodes.label: US strikes against Iran
evidence: the US stepped up military strikes against Iran

nary_nodes.label: Houthi attack on tankers
evidence: Prices spiked after Houthi militia in Yemen attacked oil tankers in the Red Sea

nary_nodes.label: Gas prices rise
evidence: Gas prices have also risen steadily over the past month

nary_nodes.label: US-Iran ceasefire
evidence: Oil prices had been falling following a temporary ceasefire between the US and Iran.

nary_nodes.label: Ceasefire fails
evidence: However, the ceasefire has failed

nary_nodes.label: Rubio says Iran not ready
evidence: this week US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the people in charge in Iran were "not ready to make a deal".

nary_nodes.label: UK petrol prices rise
evidence: New data released on Thursday showed that UK petrol prices have risen by 5p a litre since the beginning of July

nary_nodes.label: US gasoline prices surpass $4
evidence: Average gasoline prices in the US have surpassed $4 a gallon once more

nary_nodes.label: Raymond warns of ripple effects
evidence: "More expensive fuel and energy can ripple through the wider economy, increasing costs for businesses and ultimately feeding through into the price of food and other goods," said Jonathan Raymond, investment manager at Quilter Cheviot.

nary_nodes.label: Dales predicts rate hold
evidence: Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said he believed the Bank will "almost certainly" hold them again.

nary_nodes.label: Warsh vows no tolerance
evidence: Kevin Warsh, the newly-appointed chair of the US Federal Reserve, last week told Congress that the central bank had "no tolerance to persistently elevated inflation".

nary_nodes.label: Trump demands rate cuts
evidence: Trump has made it clear he expects Warsh to fulfil his demand for reductions in borrowing costs for Americans.

nary_nodes.label: Fed holds rates
evidence: But the Fed held US interest rates between 3.5% and 3.75% at Warsh's first meeting last month.

nary_nodes.label: Bank of England holds rates
evidence: The Bank of England, which sets UK interest rates, has held them at 3.75% in its last four meetings.

nary_nodes.label: Oil prices fall
evidence: They dropped back to levels last seen before the US and Israel began military action against Iran on 28 February.

nary_nodes.label: US and Israel begin action
evidence: They dropped back to levels last seen before the US and Israel began military action against Iran on 28 February.
